title: Black Forest Gateau
subtitle: German chocolate sponge with cream and cherries
excerpt: Layers of rich chocolate sponge soaked in cherry liqueur syrup, sandwiched with whipped cream and black cherries, and finished with cream rosettes and chocolate shavings.

recipe.sourceNotes: Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte (Black Forest cherry cake) is a German cream cake from the Black Forest region of Baden-Württemberg, where sour Morello cherries and Kirschwasser (cherry schnapps) are both regional specialities. The cake takes its name both from the region and from the traditional costume of the Black Forest, where women wore large hats with red pom-poms that the cream and cherry decoration is said to resemble. The cake is documented from at least the early twentieth century and was standardised in German food law in 2017: to be sold as Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte in Germany, a cake must contain at least 80 grams of Kirschwasser per kilogram of sponge. The British version, widely eaten since the 1970s and 1980s, typically replaces the Kirschwasser with a gentler kirsch syrup or omits the alcohol entirely. The chocolate sponge (Biskuit) is a fatless sponge enriched with cocoa.

recipeTools.notes: Two 20 cm round, loose-bottomed cake tins.

content.text: The sponge is a génoise-style fatless sponge whisked over warm water: the eggs and sugar are warmed together until the sugar dissolves before whisking to a very thick, pale foam. The flour and cocoa are folded in with a large metal spoon in as few strokes as possible to preserve the air. The sponge must be completely cold before splitting and assembling. Soak the cut surfaces generously with the kirsch syrup: the sponge should be moist but not soggy.

Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line two 20 cm cake tins. Whisk the eggs and sugar in a bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water for 5 minutes until thick, pale, and tripled in volume. Remove from the heat. Sift the flour and cocoa over the mixture and fold in gently with a large metal spoon. Divide between the tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.

Make the syrup: combine the reserved cherry juice, sugar, and kirsch in a small saucepan and heat until the sugar dissolves. Cool. Split each cold sponge in half horizontally to give 4 layers. Brush each cut surface generously with the kirsch syrup.

Assemble: spread a layer of whipped cream on one sponge round. Scatter over half the cherries. Top with the next sponge layer. Repeat for 4 layers. Cover the top and sides of the cake with the remaining cream. Make chocolate shavings by running a vegetable peeler along the edge of the chocolate and arrange over the top with any remaining cherries. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
